title: Boundary Handling
text: Standard LOESS neighbourhoods become asymmetric boundaries: fewer points exist one side, pulling local fit toward data interior. boundary_policy parameter controls data padded mitigate effect.

title: Boundary Handling
text: Pads beyond endpoints replicating first last observed values. Prevents fit curling toward zero safe default nearly use cases. Use : strong prior boundary behaviour; general-purpose smoothing.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Loess(boundary_policy = "extend") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4897657

title: Boundary Handling
text: Mirrors data endpoints fitting, discards reflected region output. Preserves continuity derivatives endpoints. Use : Circular data (e.g., angle, day--year), symmetric physical quantities, derivative boundary expected zero.

title: LOESS Concepts
text: LOESS (Locally Estimated Scatterplot Smoothing) nonparametric regression method fits smooth curves scatter plots without assuming global functional form. Unlike parametric methods (linear regression, polynomial fitting), LOESS adapts locally data structure, making ideal : Exploratory data analysis — Discover patterns without assumptions Trend estimation — Extract signals noisy time series Baseline correction — Remove systematic effects spectroscopy Genomic smoothing — Smooth methylation, ChIP-seq, expression data

text: point data, LOESS: Selects neighbors — Choose nearest points (controlled fraction) Assigns weights — Closer points get higher weights (using kernel function) Fits locally — Perform weighted least squares regression Extracts value — Use fitted value smoothed estimate Iterates (optional) — Reweight points based residuals reduce outlier influence

title: Custom Weights
text: Standard LOESS assigns equal prior trust observations. Custom weights let override assumption point point — distance robustness weighting applied. effective weight observation jj local fit centred xix_i : wij=custom_weights[j]×K(dijhi)×rjw_{ij} = \text{custom\_weights}[j] \times K\!\left(\frac{d_{ij}}{h_i}\right) \times r_j KK distance kernel, hih_i local bandwidth, rjr_j robustness weight current iteration. Batch adapter : custom_weights applies Batch mode. silently ignored Streaming Online adapters.

title: Custom Weights
text: mechanisms handle unreliable data, serve different purposes: compose: can use simultaneously. Custom weights suppress priori bad points; robustness iterations handle residual outliers remain.

title: Custom Weights
text: Set weight 0 bad point — excluded every local fit otherwise include .
code: library(rfastloess)  x <- 0:9 y <- x * 2.0 y[6] <- 100.0               # spike at index 5 (0-based)  weights <- rep(1.0, 10) weights[6] <- 0.0            # exclude the spike  model <- Loess(fraction = 0.5, iterations = 0L) result <- fit(model, x, y, custom_weights = weights) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.572621

title: Custom Weights
text: Assign high weights measurements trust — calibration standards, reference instruments, low-noise observations.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3) calibration_indices <- c(6, 21, 41, 61, 81)  weights <- rep(1.0, length(x)) weights[calibration_indices] <- 10.0   # trust calibration 10x more  model <- Loess(fraction = 0.5) result <- fit(model, x, y, custom_weights = weights) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4228696

title: Custom Weights
text: observation known standard deviation σi\sigma_i, set wi=1/σi2w_i = 1 / \sigma_i^2 give fit information-theoretically optimal weighting.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  sigma <- runif(100, 0.1, 0.5) weights <- 1 / sigma^2  model <- Loess(fraction = 0.5) result <- fit(model, x, y, custom_weights = weights) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4414661

title: Polynomial Degree
text: fit point weighted mean. Produces smooth results ignores local slope, introducing bias wherever true function changes. Use : Maximum smoothness matters accuracy; computationally cheapest.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Loess(degree = "constant", fraction = 0.5) result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (constant/Nadaraya-Watson):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (constant/Nadaraya-Watson): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4694689 0.4748509 0.4785029 0.4798484 0.4836073 0.4936813

title: Polynomial Degree
text: Fits weighted line neighbourhood. Removes first-order bias handles boundary regions correctly. right choice vast majority applications. Use : Default; monotone gently curved data; boundary accuracy matters.
code: model <- Loess(degree = "linear", fraction = 0.5) result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (linear local regression):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (linear local regression): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4758389 0.4846388 0.4944609 0.5054102 0.5169758 0.5286606

title: Polynomial Degree
text: Fits weighted parabola. Captures curvature data reduces bias regions strong local curvature, cost higher variance. Use : Data visible curvature local extrema; use larger fraction stabilise fit.
code: model <- Loess(degree = "quadratic", fraction = 0.5) result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (quadratic local regression):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (quadratic local regression): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4043043 0.4131994 0.4244604 0.4384709 0.4565813 0.4791656

title: Polynomial Degree
text: Fits weighted cubic polynomial. Captures inflections fine structure requires sufficiently large neighbourhood remain stable. Use : Data clear S-shaped curves multiple inflection points; use fraction >= 0.5.
code: model <- Loess(degree = "cubic", fraction = 0.6) result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (cubic local regression):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (cubic local regression): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4183075 0.4299695 0.4442197 0.4608883 0.4798054 0.5008015

title: Polynomial Degree
text: Fits weighted quartic polynomial. Rarely needed practice; useful capturing highly oscillatory local structure. prone overfitting. Use : Fine oscillatory structure physically meaningful dataset large; always cross-validate.
code: model <- Loess(degree = "quartic", fraction = 0.7) result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (quartic local regression):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (quartic local regression): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.3964750 0.4064069 0.4182002 0.4319700 0.4478315 0.4658997

title: Polynomial Degree
text: dataset boundary, neighbourhood one-sided may contain enough points support requested degree. Setting boundary_degree_fallback = TRUE automatically reduces degree boundaries avoid instability.
code: model <- Loess(degree = 2L, boundary_degree_fallback = TRUE) result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (quadratic, boundary fallback):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (quadratic, boundary fallback): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4577829 0.4682789 0.4793020 0.4908341 0.5028573 0.5153538

title: Polynomial Degree
text: Rule thumb: Start degree = 1 (default). Move degree = 2 see systematic bias regions high curvature, increase fraction time.

title: Multivariate LOESS
text: Standard LOESS operates single predictor x. Setting dimensions > 1 extends neighbourhood search local polynomial fit n-dimensional predictor space, enabling surface smoothing spatial grids, time–altitude combinations, similar multi-predictor datasets. Note: Neighbourhood search scales number dimensions. d ≥ 3 keep fraction small consider "interpolation" surface mode (default) reduce computation.

title: Multivariate LOESS
text: Single predictor. configuration required.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 10, length.out = 200) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(200, sd = 0.2)  model <- Loess(fraction = 0.3) result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (1D LOESS):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (1D LOESS): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.3808654 0.3912167 0.4028709 0.4154835 0.4286045 0.4422857

title: Multivariate LOESS
text: Two predictors (e.g., latitude/longitude, time/altitude). Pass n × 2 matrix x.
code: set.seed(42) n <- 100 lat <- runif(n, -pi, pi) lon <- runif(n, -pi, pi) z   <- sin(lat) + cos(lon) + rnorm(n, sd = 0.1)  x2d <- cbind(lat, lon)   # n × 2 matrix  model <- Loess(fraction = 0.3, dimensions = 2L) result <- fit(model, x2d, z) cat("First 6 smoothed values (2D LOESS, lat/lon):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (2D LOESS, lat/lon): print(head(result$y)) #> [1]  0.17983519  0.02191686 -0.01849028  0.22186652  0.09969107 -0.22507546

title: Multivariate LOESS
text: Pass n × d matrix x. Higher dimensions require larger fraction keep local neighbourhood populated.
code: set.seed(42) n <- 200 x1 <- runif(n) x2 <- runif(n) x3 <- runif(n) y  <- x1 + sin(2 * pi * x2) + x3^2 + rnorm(n, sd = 0.1)  x3d <- cbind(x1, x2, x3)   # n × 3 matrix  model <- Loess(fraction = 0.5, dimensions = 3L) result <- fit(model, x3d, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (3D LOESS):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (3D LOESS): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.8070023 0.9764349 0.8780069 1.0434288 0.9838051 0.8222218

title: Multivariate LOESS
text: dimensions > 1 can also control inter-point distances computed.
code: # Reuse the 2D spatial data from above; upweight the lat dimension model <- Loess(     fraction = 0.3,     dimensions = 2L,     distance_metric = "weighted",     weighted_metric_weights = c(2.0, 1.0)  # lat counts twice ) result <- fit(model, x2d, z) cat("First 6 smoothed values (2D LOESS, weighted distance):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (2D LOESS, weighted distance): print(head(result$y)) #> [1]  0.17709387  0.08359416 -0.05142187  0.14223791  0.12033868 -0.13208634

title: Multivariate LOESS
text: large 2D 3D datasets use "interpolation" (default) tune cell interpolation_vertices control grid resolution.

title: Confidence and Prediction Intervals
text: Adapter support: Confidence prediction intervals available Batch mode . Streaming Online modes support intervals.

title: Confidence and Prediction Intervals
text: Estimate uncertainty smoothed curve .
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Loess(fraction = 0.5, confidence_intervals = 0.95) result <- fit(model, x, y)  # Plot with bands plot(x, y, pch = 16, col = "gray",     main = "LOESS with 95% Confidence Intervals") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2) lines(result$x, result$confidence_lower, col = "blue", lty = 2) lines(result$x, result$confidence_upper, col = "blue", lty = 2) cat("95% CI at midpoint: [", result$confidence_lower[50], ", ",     result$confidence_upper[50], "]\n") #> 95% CI at midpoint: [ -0.102212 ,  0.1763286 ]

title: Confidence and Prediction Intervals
text: Estimate new observations might fall.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Loess(fraction = 0.5, prediction_intervals = 0.95) result <- fit(model, x, y)  plot(x, y, pch = 16, col = "gray",     main = "LOESS with 95% Prediction Intervals") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2) lines(result$x, result$prediction_lower, col = "red", lty = 2) lines(result$x, result$prediction_upper, col = "red", lty = 2) cat("Prediction bounds: [", result$prediction_lower[1], ", ",     result$prediction_upper[1], "]\n") #> Prediction bounds: [ -0.1439302 ,  1.095608 ]

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Weight functions (kernels) determine neighboring points contribute local fit. Points closer target receive higher weights.

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Efficiency = AMISE relative Epanechnikov (1.0 = optimal)

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Cleveland’s original choice. Best -around performance. w(u)=(1−|u|3)3w(u) = (1 - |u|^3)^3 Use : Default choice applications.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Loess(weight_function = "tricube") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4897657

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Theoretically optimal kernel density estimation. w(u)=34(1−u2)w(u) = \frac{3}{4}(1 - u^2) Use : Optimal MSE properties desired.
code: model <- Loess(weight_function = "epanechnikov") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4827792

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Infinitely smooth. boundary effects. w(u)=exp⁡(−u2/2)w(u) = \exp(-u^2/2) Use : Maximum smoothness needed, computational cost acceptable.
code: model <- Loess(weight_function = "gaussian") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4666483

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Good balance efficiency smoothness. w(u)=(1−u2)2w(u) = (1 - u^2)^2 Use : Alternative Tricube slightly different properties.
code: model <- Loess(weight_function = "biweight") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4880718

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Smooth computationally efficient. w(u)=cos⁡(πu/2)w(u) = \cos(\pi u / 2) Use : Want smooth kernel simple form.
code: model <- Loess(weight_function = "cosine") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4829559

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Simple linear taper. w(u)=1−|u|w(u) = 1 - |u| Use : Simple, interpretable weights.
code: model <- Loess(weight_function = "triangle") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4849057

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Equal weights within window. Fastest least smooth. w(u)=1w(u) = 1 Use : Speed critical, smoothness less important.
code: model <- Loess(weight_function = "uniform") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4678518

text: Streaming LOESS processes data fixed-size chunks configurable overlap. Points inside overlap zone receive estimates adjacent chunks; merge strategy decides two estimates reconciled.

title: Merge Strategies
text: Takes arithmetic mean left-chunk right-chunk estimates overlap region. Fast sufficient chunks similar smoothing quality. Use : Chunks large overlap region uniform data density.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- StreamingLoess(     merge_strategy = "average",     chunk_size = 60,     overlap = 20 ) invisible(process_chunk(model, x[1:60], y[1:60])) # The second chunk's overlap region (its first 20 points) is where # merge_strategy actually blends the two chunks' estimates. result <- process_chunk(model, x[61:100], y[61:100]) cat("Merged value in overlap region (average):\n") #> Merged value in overlap region (average): print(result$y[6]) #> [1] 0.2286069

title: Merge Strategies
text: Keeps left-chunk estimate overlap zone discards right-chunk estimate. Produces left-flush output. Use : need final output values immediately chunk (look-ahead revision); left-chunk context dominates.
code: model <- StreamingLoess(     merge_strategy = "take_first",     chunk_size = 60,     overlap = 20 ) invisible(process_chunk(model, x[1:60], y[1:60])) result <- process_chunk(model, x[61:100], y[61:100]) cat("Merged value in overlap region (take_first):\n") #> Merged value in overlap region (take_first): print(result$y[6]) #> [1] 0.236299

title: Merge Strategies
text: Keeps right-chunk estimate overlap zone. right chunk sees surrounding data, estimates can accurate overlap region. Use : Right-chunk context improves overlap quality; post-processing complete data rather streaming real time.
code: model <- StreamingLoess(     merge_strategy = "take_last",     chunk_size = 60,     overlap = 20 ) invisible(process_chunk(model, x[1:60], y[1:60])) result <- process_chunk(model, x[61:100], y[61:100]) cat("Merged value in overlap region (take_last):\n") #> Merged value in overlap region (take_last): print(result$y[6]) #> [1] 0.2209148

title: Merge Strategies
text: Assigns overlap point weight proportional proximity centre respective chunk: points near left-chunk centre favour left estimate; points near right-chunk centre favour right. Minimises boundary artefacts. Use : Minimising boundary artefacts important speed; moderate overlap (10–20% chunk size) used.
code: model <- StreamingLoess(     merge_strategy = "weighted_average",     chunk_size = 60,     overlap = 20 ) invisible(process_chunk(model, x[1:60], y[1:60])) result <- process_chunk(model, x[61:100], y[61:100]) cat("Merged value in overlap region (weighted_average):\n") #> Merged value in overlap region (weighted_average): print(result$y[6]) #> [1] 0.232453

title: Merge Strategies
text: Overlap size matters: larger overlap gives merge strategy room blend, reducing boundary artefacts regardless strategy chosen. good starting point 10% chunk_size.

title: Robustness
text: Standard LOESS can biased outliers. Robustness iterations downweight points large residuals: Fit initial LOESS Compute residuals Assign robustness weights (large residuals → low weight) Refit using combined distance × robustness weights Repeat steps 2–4

title: Robustness
text: Smooth downweighting. Points transition gradually full weight zero. w(u)={(1−u2)2|u|<10|u|≥1w(u) = \begin{cases} (1 - u^2)^2 & |u| < 1 \\ 0 & |u| \geq 1 \end{cases} Use : General purpose, balanced approach.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Loess(iterations = 3, robustness_method = "bisquare") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4897657

title: Robustness
text: Linear penalty beyond threshold. Less aggressive Bisquare. w(u)={1|u|≤kk/|u||u|>kw(u) = \begin{cases} 1 & |u| \leq k \\ k/|u| & |u| > k \end{cases} Use : Moderate outliers, want retain influence.
code: model <- Loess(iterations = 3, robustness_method = "huber") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4999039

title: Robustness
text: Hard threshold. Points either fully weighted completely excluded. w(u)={1|u|≤k0|u|>kw(u) = \begin{cases} 1 & |u| \leq k \\ 0 & |u| > k \end{cases} Use : Extreme outliers, want binary exclusion.
code: model <- Loess(iterations = 3, robustness_method = "talwar") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4730281

title: Scaling Methods
text: iterations > 0, LOESS computes robustness weights comparing residual current residual scale estimate σ̂\hat{\sigma}. scaling_method parameter controls σ̂\hat{\sigma} estimated. wi=B(|ri|6⋅σ̂)w_i = B\!\left(\frac{|r_i|}{6 \cdot \hat{\sigma}}\right)

title: Scaling Methods
text: σ̂=median(|ri−median(ri)|)\hat{\sigma} = \text{median}(|r_i - \text{median}(r_i)|) First centers residuals median, takes median absolute deviations. Double use median makes highly resistant extreme outliers. Use : Data may contain outliers (default applications).
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Loess(iterations = 3, scaling_method = "mad") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4897657

title: Scaling Methods
text: σ̂=median(|ri|)\hat{\sigma} = \text{median}(|r_i|) Uses uncentered median — unlike MAD subtract residual median first. Still robust (median-based), faster (one partial sort instead two). Use : Speed matters data minimal systematic bias residuals.
code: model <- Loess(iterations = 3, scaling_method = "mar") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.5096452

title: Scaling Methods
text: σ̂=1n∑|ri|\hat{\sigma} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i |r_i| Arithmetic mean absolute residuals. Non-robust: single extreme outlier inflates σ̂\hat{\sigma}, causing bisquare weight function -downweight outliers. Use : Clean data outliers; maximum computation speed required.
code: model <- Loess(iterations = 3, scaling_method = "mean") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.512746

title: Use Case: Genomic Data Smoothing
text: small fraction = 0.1 lets LOESS follow fine-scale spatial structure without smearing transitions methylated unmethylated regions. confidence_intervals = 0.95 produces uncertainty bands naturally widen positions sparser CpG coverage, making low-confidence segments immediately apparent plot.
code: library(rfastloess)  set.seed(42) n <- 1000 positions <- sort(runif(n, 0, 1e6))  true_meth <- 0.5 + 0.3 * sin(positions / 1e5) observed  <- true_meth + rnorm(n, sd = 0.15) observed  <- pmax(0, pmin(1, observed))  model <- Loess(     fraction = 0.1,     iterations = 3,     confidence_intervals = 0.95 ) result <- fit(model, positions, observed)  plot(positions, observed, pch = ".", col = "gray",     xlab = "Genomic Position (bp)", ylab = "Methylation Level",     main = "Methylation Profile Smoothing") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2) lines(result$x, result$confidence_lower, col = "blue", lty = 2) lines(result$x, result$confidence_upper, col = "blue", lty = 2) legend("topright", c("Observed", "Smoothed", "95% CI"),         pch = c(1, NA, NA), lty = c(NA, 1, 2),         col = c("gray", "blue", "blue"))

title: Use Case: Genomic Data Smoothing
text: ChIP-seq experiments produce sparse, noisy coverage data. LOESS can help identify binding regions. fraction = 0.05 provides high spatial resolution — important resolving narrow binding peaks otherwise smeared background. larger iterations = 5 deliberate: Poisson-distributed read counts produce tall, isolated spikes, extra robustness iterations progressively -weight estimated background level inflated handful extreme counts.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(123)  positions <- seq(0, 9990, by = 10) n <- length(positions)  background <- 10 peak1 <- 50 * exp(-((positions - 2000)^2) / (2 * 200^2)) peak2 <- 80 * exp(-((positions - 5000)^2) / (2 * 300^2)) peak3 <- 40 * exp(-((positions - 8000)^2) / (2 * 150^2))  true_signal <- background + peak1 + peak2 + peak3 observed <- rpois(n, true_signal)  model <- Loess(     fraction = 0.05,   # Very local smoothing     iterations = 5,    # Strong robustness     return_residuals = TRUE ) result <- fit(model, positions, observed)  # Identify peaks (smoothed signal significantly above background) threshold <- quantile(result$y, 0.75) peaks <- positions[result$y > threshold] cat(sprintf("Found %d peak positions (first 5): %s\n",             length(peaks), toString(head(peaks, 5)))) #> Found 250 peak positions (first 5): 1630, 1640, 1650, 1660, 1670

title: Use Case: Real-Time Processing
text: data arrives continuously — sensors, logs, streaming pipelines — need incremental smoothing doesn’t require reprocessing entire dataset.

title: Use Case: Real-Time Processing
text: true real-time applications point must processed immediately. window_capacity = 25 limits internal buffer 25 recent observations; add_point call costs O(window) rather growing total history. min_points = 5 suppresses output window holds enough points stable fit — calls made threshold return NULL. update_mode = "incremental" re-fits recent point rather full window, halving typical latency modest accuracy cost.

title: Use Case: Real-Time Processing
code: library(rfastloess)  set.seed(42) times        <- 1:100 temperatures <- 20 + 5 * sin(times / 10) + rnorm(100)  model <- OnlineLoess(     fraction = 0.3,     window_capacity = 25,     min_points = 5,     update_mode = "incremental" ) for (i in seq_along(times)) {     result <- add_point(model, times[i], temperatures[i])     if (!is.null(result))         cat(sprintf("Time %d: %.2f\n", times[i], result$y))     if (i >= 10) break  # print only the first few outputs } #> Time 5: 22.80 #> Time 6: 22.72 #> Time 7: 24.73 #> Time 8: 23.49 #> Time 9: 25.94 #> Time 10: 24.14

title: Use Case: Real-Time Processing
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) n      <- 200 times  <- seq_len(n) signal <- 10 + 2 * sin(times / 20) + rnorm(n, sd = 1)  model <- OnlineLoess(     fraction        = 0.3,     window_capacity = 30,     min_points      = 5 )  smoothed_x <- numeric(n) smoothed_y <- numeric(n) n_out <- 0L  for (i in seq_len(n)) {     result <- add_point(model, times[i], signal[i])     if (!is.null(result)) {         n_out <- n_out + 1L         smoothed_x[n_out] <- times[i]         smoothed_y[n_out] <- result$y     } }  smoothed_x <- smoothed_x[seq_len(n_out)] smoothed_y <- smoothed_y[seq_len(n_out)]  plot(times, signal, pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = "gray",     xlab = "Time", ylab = "Value",     main = "Online LOESS — Accumulated Output") lines(smoothed_x, smoothed_y, col = "blue", lwd = 2)

title: Use Case: Real-Time Processing
text: large datasets arrive batches files. chunk_size controls many data points processed one pass; matching file-read buffer message-batch size avoids unnecessary copying. overlap retains many points previous chunk context neighbourhood chunk boundaries artificially truncated. merge_strategy = "weighted_average" blends overlapping region smoothly; use "take_last" chunk boundaries guaranteed well separated blending needed. Always call finalize(): streaming adapter buffers overlap data. Call finalize(model) last chunk retrieve buffered tail.

title: Use Case: Real-Time Processing
text: dashboard pattern uses plain LOESS fit manually managed sliding window rather OnlineLoess. simplest approach UI framework already owns data buffer need recent smoothed value per frame. trade-full O(window^2) refit every tick; high-frequency streams prefer OnlineLoess update_mode = "incremental" bound per-frame cost.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42)  window_capacity <- 50 data_x <- numeric(0) data_y <- numeric(0)  for (i in 0:199) {     xi <- i     yi <- 25.0 + 10 * sin(i / 20) + rnorm(1, sd = 2)     data_x <- c(data_x, xi)     data_y <- c(data_y, yi)      if (length(data_x) > window_capacity) {         data_x <- tail(data_x, window_capacity)         data_y <- tail(data_y, window_capacity)     }      if (length(data_x) >= 5) {         model <- Loess(fraction = 0.4)         result <- fit(model, data_x, data_y)         current_smoothed <- tail(result$y, 1)     } }

title: Use Case: Time Series Analysis
text: fraction = 0.1 sizes neighbourhood 10% data evaluation point — narrow enough follow slowly varying trend without smearing periodic variation. Three robustness iterations -weight noise spikes bias fitted curve; especially important signal--noise ratio low occasional outliers expected.
code: library(rfastloess)  set.seed(42) t <- seq(0, 100, length.out = 500) trend <- 10 + 0.5 * t + 3 * sin(t / 10) noise <- rnorm(500, sd = 3) y <- trend + noise  model <- Loess(fraction = 0.1, iterations = 3) result <- fit(model, t, y)  plot(t, y, col = "gray", pch = ".",     xlab = "Time", ylab = "Value", main = "Trend Extraction") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2) legend("topleft", c("Observed", "Trend (LOESS)"),         pch = c(1, NA), lty = c(NA, 1), col = c("gray", "blue"))

title: Use Case: Time Series Analysis
text: Setting return_residuals = TRUE stores observed − smoothed alongside smooth. slightly wider fraction = 0.4 produces smoother baseline trend, short-duration oscillations end residuals rather absorbed trend component. residual series ready spectral analysis, seasonality detection, change-point methods.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42)  t        <- 1:120 trend    <- 100 + 0.5 * t seasonal <- 15 * sin(2 * pi * t / 12) noise    <- rnorm(120, sd = 5) y        <- trend + seasonal + noise  model    <- Loess(fraction = 0.4, iterations = 2) result   <- fit(model, t, y) residual <- y - result$y  par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 0.5)) plot(t, y, type = "l", col = "gray",     main = "Original + LOESS Trend", xlab = "Month", ylab = "Value") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2)  plot(t, residual, type = "l", col = "darkgreen",     main = "Detrended Residual (Seasonal Component)",     xlab = "Month", ylab = "Residual") abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "red") par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

title: Use Case: Time Series Analysis
text: Prediction intervals widen uncertainty band include uncertainty fitted curve (confidence interval) expected scatter new observations around . fraction = 0.2 offers balance local detail stable interval width — small fraction produces jagged interval edges; large fraction underestimates local variance near turning points.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) t <- seq(0, 100, length.out = 500) y <- 10 + 0.3 * t + sin(t / 5) + rnorm(500, sd = 2)  model <- Loess(     fraction = 0.2,     iterations = 3,     confidence_intervals = 0.95,     prediction_intervals = 0.95 ) result <- fit(model, t, y)  plot(t, y, pch = ".", col = "gray",     xlab = "Time", ylab = "Value",     main = "Trend with 95% Prediction Interval") polygon(c(result$x, rev(result$x)),         c(result$prediction_upper, rev(result$prediction_lower)),         col = rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.15), border = NA) lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2)

text: LOESS naturally handles irregular time sampling:
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42)  t_irregular <- sort(runif(200, 0, 100)) y_irregular <- 10 + t_irregular * 0.3 + rnorm(200, sd = 2)  model <- Loess(fraction = 0.2) result <- fit(model, t_irregular, y_irregular) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 12.10549

title: Use Case: Time Series Analysis
text: Use different fractions extract features different scales:
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) t <- seq(0, 100, length.out = 500) trend_true <- 10 + 0.5 * t + 3 * sin(t / 10) y <- trend_true + rnorm(length(t), sd = 3)  fractions <- c(0.05, 0.2, 0.5)  plot(t, y, col = "gray", pch = ".",     xlab = "Time", ylab = "Value", main = "Multi-Scale LOESS")  for (f in fractions) {     model <- Loess(fraction = f)     result <- fit(model, t, y)     lines(result$x, result$y, lwd = 2) } legend("topleft", paste0("fraction=", fractions), lty = 1)

title: Use Case: Time Series Analysis
text: Biological application:
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42)  hours <- seq(0, 24, by = 0.5) expression <- 100 * (1 + 0.5 * sin(hours * pi / 12)) +     rnorm(length(hours), sd = 10)  model <- Loess(     fraction = 0.3,     iterations = 3,     confidence_intervals = 0.95,     return_diagnostics = TRUE ) result <- fit(model, hours, expression)  cat("R2:", result$diagnostics$r_squared, "\n") #> R2: 0.9096872
